about: What SecuRAX claims, the conditions each claim holds under (its envelope), and the test or real-stack journey that proves it. `./securax fitness` fails if any proof goes missing, so the docs cannot drift into marketing. Evidence forms: 'test:<path>::<function>' (a pytest function), 'file:<path>' (a test script), 'journey:<name>' (sandbox/run.py, runs the real estate in CI).

claims.claim: Cross-device sync converges: the same edits arriving in any order, any number of times, give the same state on every device and the server.
claims.envelope: Per-key last-writer-wins (a whole localStorage key is the unit; there is no per-item merge inside one key). Client clocks are corrected by the server's Date header. One SQLite file on one host.

claims.claim: Concurrent saves from several devices never erase each other's changes.
claims.envelope: Proven with 8 concurrent writers on separate connections against one SQLite file on local disk (WAL, an immediate write lock). Not for SQLite on network storage.

claims.claim: Malformed sync input is refused with a clear error, never a crash, and never changes stored data.
claims.envelope: Bodies up to the size limit; JSON objects only; timestamps must be non-negative numbers.

claims.claim: An update backs up first and, when the new version does not start healthy, returns to the version that worked with the data intact.
claims.envelope: A git checkout without uncommitted local changes; Docker running.

claims.claim: Backups are verified when written and restore to a working estate, encrypted or not; a wrong key or a tampered file is refused.
claims.envelope: Docker volumes of this estate on one host; models are not included (re-downloadable).

claims.claim: When a safety detector is offline and FAIL_MODE is closed, the gateway refuses instead of letting unchecked text through, and says why.
claims.envelope: The gateway is the only path to models (BUILD-CONTRACT invariant).

claims.claim: Every model chain ends in the local model, so an answer is possible with zero keys and no internet.
claims.envelope: The local model is small on a laptop: slower and weaker than cloud models.

claims.claim: You stay signed in to Chat after an update recreates its container.
A crashed service is restarted and the failure is reported.
The people-scale ladder never promises a tier the repository cannot evidence; what is dormant or missing is listed.
claims.envelope: Planning output, not a load test.

not_claimed: High availability or multi-region: every service runs once, on one host. A host outage is an outage; recovery is restore-from-backup.
Horizontal scale of the sync service: one SQLite file. Correct with many workers on that host, not across hosts.
Team chat at scale (presence, message ordering across thousands of users, search over billions of messages): Mattermost is an optional pinned organ, not something SecuRAX built.
Load-tested capacity beyond the measured fitness budgets: the capacity planner is planning, not a benchmark.
Model quality: answers come from third-party or small local models; the rails reduce risk, they do not make answers correct.
An independent security audit or certification (SOC 2, ISO 27001): none has been done.
Multi-tenant production (the forest stage): manifests render and validate; billing, per-tenant SSO and operations are not built.
